end.summary:
Practised showing numbers 11–20 as one ten and some ones.
Used a full row or bundle of ten, then counted the loose ones.
Saanvi correctly identified 14 as one ten and four ones and 17 as one ten and seven ones.
Saanvi first suggested two tens for 15, then stated one ten and some ones.
Teach-back was not passed; 1 of 2 attempts was unaided correct.
end.parentNote: Saanvi practised making numbers 11–20 with one full group of ten and loose ones. Counting the full ten-row first helped, and they later used one ten and seven ones for 17. There was a mix-up about whether 15 has two tens; it was corrected later by stating one ten and some ones. At home, show a number from 11–20 with objects and ask, “How many tens? How many ones?”
